parole.significato: The central seed or "germinating matrix" of a culture.
parole.testo: From Swahili asili (“origin”); introduced in this sense by Marimba Ani.

parole.significato: A member of a local African military or police unit, usually one serving in a European colonial force.
parole.testo: From Swahili askari (“soldier”), from Arabic عَسْكَرِيّ (ʕaskariyy). Doublet of lascar.

parole.significato: A mancala board game played in East Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili bao.

parole.significato: A council or assembly in parts of East Africa.
parole.testo: From Swahili baraza.

parole.significato: A bicycle or motorcycle used as a taxi.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili bodaboda, from English border.

parole.significato: An enclosure usually made of thorn bushes, and latterly of steel fencing, for protection from marauders.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili boma (“enclosure, fortified outpost”).

parole.significato: Synonym of chador (“Muslim women's garment”).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili buibui.

parole.significato: Big boss, important person.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili bwana (“master”), from Arabic أَبُونَا (ʔabūnā, “our father”). Doublet of abbot.

parole.significato: Any of several types of informal cooperative society.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili chama (“organisation, society”).

parole.significato: A kind of potato-egg omelette popular in Tanzania.
parole.testo: From Swahili chipsi mayai (literally “chips (and) eggs”).

parole.significato: Synonym of shared taxi.
parole.testo: From Swahili daladala, duplicated call of dala (“5-shilling coin”), from English dollar, q.v. Compare US dollar van.

parole.significato: Blood (a member of the Los Angeles gang the Bloods)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili damu (“blood”), borrowed from Arabic دَم (dam, “blood”), from Proto-Semitic *dam-, from Proto-Afroasiatic *dam-.

parole.significato: A medicine, particularly a native one or one used by witch doctors.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili dawa (“medicine”), borrowed from Arabic دَوَاء (dawāʔ).

parole.significato: A tin container used for kerosene etc.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili debe, borrowed from Omani Arabic دِبّة.

parole.significato: A shop, store.
parole.testo: From Swahili duka, from Arabic دُكَّان (dukkān), from Aramaic דּוּכָּנָא (dukkānā, “dais”), from Akkadian 𒆠𒍇 (/⁠takkannu, dakkannu, dukkannu⁠/, “dais, platform, bench; niche, bedroom, private chambers or quarters”), ultimately from Sumerian 𒆠𒍇 (/⁠daggan⁠/, “chamber, doorway or its frame, niche in a

parole.significato: A person who repairs and maintains things; mechanic, repairer.
parole.testo: From Swahili fundi. Ultimately from Proto-Bantu *-túnda.

parole.significato: A sack.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili gunia. Doublet of gunny.

parole.significato: No worries, take it easy.
parole.testo: From Swahili hakuna matata (“there are no problems”). Popularized in English by the 1994 Disney film The Lion King.

parole.significato: A traditional Kenyan community self-help event or organization.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili harambee.

parole.significato: haste makes waste; more haste, less speed
parole.testo: Calque of Swahili haraka haraka haina baraka

parole.significato: faith (in the context of African-American culture)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili imani (“faith”), borrowed from Arabic إِيمَان (ʔīmān), from آمَنَ (ʔāmana).

parole.significato: A kind of hoe (digging tool).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili jembe, from Proto-Bantu *ìgèmbè.

parole.significato: A portable stove of the type common in Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili jiko.

parole.significato: A woolen robe worn by Arabs.
parole.testo: Derived from Swahili joho, borrowed from Arabic جُوخ (jūḵ), borrowed from Ottoman Turkish چوقه (çuqa, çuha).

parole.significato: The informal economy; self-employment other than agriculture.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili jua kali, from jua (“sun”) + kali (“fierce”).

parole.significato: Especially large or powerful.
parole.testo: From Jumbo (1860–1885), the name given to a large African elephant from East Africa that was purchased in 1882 by American showman P. T. Barnum (1810–1891) for the Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey Circus. Compare Swahili jambo (“matter, thing”) and jumbe (“chief, headman”).

parole.significato: An uncooked dish of chopped tomatoes, onions, and chili peppers in African cuisine.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili kachumbari, borrowed from Gujarati કચુંબર (kacumbar, “kachumber”). Doublet of kachumber.

parole.significato: A child soldier. Usually refers to the eastern Congolese rebel armies that used numerous child soldiers.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili kadogo.

parole.significato: A colourful printed cotton garment worn by women in East Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili kanga, from Proto-Bantu *nkángà.

parole.significato: A white or cream-coloured robe worn by men in the African Great Lakes region.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili kanzu, borrowed from Arabic [Term?].

parole.significato: The feast eaten as part of Kwanzaa celebrations.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili karamu (“feast, banquet”).

parole.significato: A piece of colored cloth used as clothing in Africa, wrapped around the waist and legs or shoulders.
parole.testo: From Swahili kikoi.

parole.significato: Any cup used for pouring libations to honor ancestors and communal drinking at dinner during the Kwanzaa holiday
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili Kikombe cha Umoja.

parole.significato: A candle holder used in Kwanzaa celebrations.
parole.testo: From Swahili kinara (“candlestick”), ultimately from Arabic مَنَارَة (manāra).

parole.significato: A brimless cylindrical cap with a flat crown, worn by men in East Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili kofia, borrowed from Omani Arabic كُوفِيَّة. Doublet of keffiyeh.

parole.significato: A type of hartebeest from East Africa.
parole.testo: From Swahili kongoni.

parole.significato: self-determination (in the context of African-American culture)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili kujichagulia (“self-determination”).

parole.significato: A teacher of sexual topics in the Swahili unyago ritual.
parole.testo: From Swahili kungwi.

parole.significato: The history of slavery and anti-black racism and discrimination in the United States; the historical enslavement of Afr…
parole.testo: From Swahili maafa (“disaster, catastrophe”). Coined in 1994 by Marimba Ani (in Let the Circle Be Unbroken: The Implications of African Spirituality in the Diaspora) on the model of the Hebrew-derived designation Shoah of the Jewish Holocaust.

parole.significato: Metal sheeting, often corrugated iron.
parole.testo: From Swahili mabati.

parole.significato: A street vendor; a hawker.
parole.testo: From Swahili Machinga, a small ethnic group living on the southern Indian Ocean coast of Tanzania, whose members are known to work in the cities as itinerant traders.

parole.significato: The political devolution of power to the individual regions of Kenya.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili majimbo (literally “regions”).

parole.significato: The political devolution of power to the regions of a country.
parole.testo: From Swahili majimbo (“regions”) + -ism.

parole.significato: A female vegetable hawker.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili mama mboga (literally “mother vegetable”), from mama + mboga.

parole.significato: A female food hawker.
parole.testo: From Swahili mama ntilie (literally “mother put it on [my plate]”).

parole.significato: A form of fried bread from eastern Africa.
parole.testo: From Swahili mandazi.

parole.significato: A type of simple fishing vessel found on the coast of East Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili mashua (“boat”), borrowed from Omani Arabic ماشوة.

parole.significato: A minivan used as a shared taxi, especially one operating without a licence.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili matatu, from ma- + -tatu (“three”).

parole.significato: A pocket of carbon-dioxide-rich air that accumulates near the ground and can be lethal to humans and animals.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili mazuku (“evil wind”).

parole.significato: vegetable
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili mboga.

parole.significato: An African medicine man.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili mganga. Doublet of inyanga and ngaka.

parole.significato: Nine Bantu ethnic groups inhabiting the coast of Kenya.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili miji kenda (“nine villages”), from mji + kenda.

parole.significato: Second-hand clothing, especially that provided by aid agencies and subsequently sold.
parole.testo: From Swahili mitumba, plural of mtumba (“bundle, bale”). Second-hand clothes are often packaged in bundles or bales.

parole.significato: The decorative mat on which ceremonial symbols are laid out during Kwanzaa celebrations.
parole.testo: From Swahili mkeka.

parole.significato: A system of voting held in Kenya during the Moi era where voters would line up behind their favored candidates contrary…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili mlolongo (“queuing, lining up”).

parole.significato: cassava
parole.testo: Derived from Swahili muhogo, borrowed from Omani Arabic مْهوجه (mhōgo), possibly from Portuguese mandioca, borrowed from Old Tupi mandi'oka, from Proto-Tupi-Guarani *maniʔok, from Proto-Tupian *mani (“cassava”) + Proto-Tupi-Guarani *ʔok (“tuber”).

parole.significato: Synonym of African blackwood
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili mpingo.

parole.significato: The name used in the 19th and early 20th centuries for a poisonous tree native to Mozambique whose bark was being studi…
parole.testo: From Swahili mwavi or a cognate in some other Bantu language.

parole.significato: Iroko (Milicia excelsa), a tropical African tree yielding valuable wood.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili mvule.

parole.significato: A teacher in parts of Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili mwalimu.

parole.significato: An elder (old person).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili mzee.

parole.significato: A white person.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili mzungu, from Common Bantu *mʊ̀díʊ́ngʊ̀.

parole.significato: A large social dancing event in parts of Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili ngoma (“dance”).

parole.significato: barbecued beef
parole.testo: From Swahili nyama ya kuchoma.

parole.significato: A person's precedent or example.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili nyayo (“footsteps, footprints”), from Proto-Bantu [Term?].

parole.significato: A large broad-bladed knife.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili panga (“machete”).

parole.significato: A tree of the African species Millettia stuhlmannii, or its wood.
parole.testo: From Swahili mpangapanga, possibly indirectly via a language of a colonial power.

parole.significato: A secret trail or road used for illegal activities such as smuggling.
parole.testo: From Swahili panya (“rat”) + route.

parole.significato: An African beer made from millet.
parole.testo: From Swahili pombe (“beer”).

parole.significato: A food product made of cornmeal.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili posho, itself from English portion.

parole.significato: A wooden throwing club or baton used in certain East African tribal cultures.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili rungu.

parole.significato: A trip into any undeveloped area to see, photograph or to hunt wild animals in their own environment.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili safari (“journey”), borrowed from Arabic سَفَر (safar).

parole.significato: To send credit using the Sambaza system; (generally) to send or share something.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili sambaza (“to disperse, scatter”), popularized by Sambaza, a credit sharing service developed by Kenyan mobile network operator Safaricom in 2005.

parole.significato: A white calico shroud used in East Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili sanda, borrowed from Arabic سَنْد (sand).

parole.significato: Any of several small, insectivorous long-nosed mammals, of the family Macroscelididae within the Macroscelidea order, n…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili sengi, probably from another Bantu language (compare Giryama sanje).

parole.significato: A coin, one hundredth of a Tanzanian shilling.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili senti, borrowed from English cent.

parole.significato: An area of cultivated ground; a plot of land, a small subsistence farm for growing crops and fruit-bearing trees, often…
parole.testo: From Swahili shamba.

parole.significato: A consultation, usually between a bwana and a local African.
parole.testo: From Swahili shauri, borrowed from Arabic شَوْر (šawr, “advice, counsel”).

parole.significato: A barbarian (variously used to refer to foreigners, Europeans, or pagans)
parole.testo: From Swahili -shenzi.

parole.significato: An evil spirit from East African mythology, often the subject of artwork.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili shetani, borrowed from Arabic شَيْطَان (šayṭān). Doublet of Satan and shaitan.

parole.significato: outlaw, bandit
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili shifta, from Amharic ሽፍታ (šəfta).

parole.significato: A unit of currency in East Africa, currently only in use by Tanzania, and divided into 100 senti.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili shilingi, from English shilling.

parole.significato: A sash (decorative length of cloth) worn in parts of Africa.
parole.testo: From Swahili shuka.

parole.significato: An army ant.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili siafu, from Proto-Bantu [Term?].

parole.significato: The marsh buck, Tragelaphus spekeii.
parole.testo: From Swahili.

parole.significato: A species of African ape, supposedly a variety of the chimpanzee.
parole.testo: Perhaps from Swahili sokwe (“chimpanzee, non-human hominid”).

parole.significato: A type of cooking pot popular in East Africa.
parole.testo: From Swahili [Term?], some consider it an example of translanguaging.

parole.significato: A deep metal cooking pot with a flat base and no handles.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili sufuria, borrowed from Omani Arabic صفرية (ṣufriya, “cooking pot”), from صفر (“copper”) + ـية (-iyya).

parole.significato: An East African dish of greens (especially collard greens) simmered with tomatoes.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili sukuma wiki (literally “to push the week”), from sukuma + wiki. The vegetable is generally affordable and available all-year round in East Africa. It forms part of the staple dish in this region together with ugali.

parole.significato: A member of various ethnic groups — mainly Bantu, Afro-Arab and Comorian — inhabiting the Swahili coast.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili Mswahili / Kiswahili, from Arabic سَوَاحِلِيّ (sawāḥiliyy, “(people) of the coasts”), from سَوَاحِل (sawāḥil, “coasts”), broken plural of سَاحِل (sāḥil, “coast”).

parole.significato: A genre of music popular in Tanzania and Kenya, influenced by the music of cultures with a historical presence in East…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili taarab, borrowed from Arabic طَرَب (ṭarab, “entertainment with music”).

parole.significato: An antelope of the species Damaliscus korrigum syn. Damaliscus lunatus.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili topi. From Mende ndope (“antelope”).

parole.significato: African cornmeal porridge
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili ugali, from an Eastern Sudanic language.

parole.significato: freedom
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili uhuru.

parole.significato: A socialist ideology of cooperation and collective advancement that formed the basis of socioeconomic policies in Tanza…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swahili ujamaa (“brotherhood, extended family”), from jamaa (“family”), from Arabic جَمَاعَة (jamāʕa, “group (of people)”).

parole.significato: Collective work and responsibility, in the context of African-American culture.
parole.testo: From Swahili ujima (“collective work and responsibility”).

parole.significato: In Swahili culture, a set of rituals that use music and dance to celebrate the coming of age of girls, teaching them ab…
parole.testo: From Swahili unyago.

parole.significato: A culture's vital energy, which gives it its emotional tone and motivates collective behavior.
parole.testo: From a blend of Swahili utamaduni (“culture”) and roho (“spirit”); introduced in this sense by Marimba Ani in 1994.

parole.significato: culturally structured thought or worldview
parole.testo: From a blend of Swahili utamaduni (“culture”) and wazo (“thought”); introduced in this sense by Marimba Ani in 1994.

parole.significato: A group of the Maasai people.
parole.testo: From Swahili [Term?].

parole.significato: finger millet, Eleusine coracana.
parole.testo: From Swahili wimbi.

parole.significato: A stringed instrument of sub-Saharan Africa.
parole.testo: From Swahili zeze.

parole.significato: A genre of urban East African music recorded in the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s.
parole.testo: From Swahili zilizopendwa (“those that were loved (inanimate)”), probably because the genre arose in the post-independence era in East Africa and was loved by locals for its representation of freedom.
